unit.title: Designing and governing agents at school

lesson.title: A school policy for agents
lesson.subtitle: Six questions, the cost, and who stays responsible

video.title: A school policy for agents
video.format_note: Animated explainer, 16:9, flat Darsi colours on paper-grey backgrounds, one recurring teacher character. Narration in the lesson language; captions as separate files, never burned in.
cast: Dr Farah Rahman — university lecturer in education, Bangladesh (main character)
Ms Amina Bello — primary teacher, Nigeria (cameo)
Mr Joseph Mwangi — computer studies teacher, Kenya (cameo)
Narrator — the Darsi voice (warm, peer to peer)

scenes.visual: A list: Three agents; Marks in the cloud; Who approves?.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: At our school, three teachers use three different agents. One pastes pupils’ marks into a cloud chatbot. Nobody knows who approves what. We need rules everyone can follow.

scenes.animation: The Darsi mark pops in; the title slides up.
scenes.narration: Today: writing your school’s policy for AI agents.

scenes.visual: A list: Which jobs?; What data?; Who approves?; Tests and records; When it goes wrong.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: A good policy answers six questions. Which jobs may agents do? What data may they see? Who approves their actions? How are they tested and recorded? And what happens when something goes wrong?

scenes.visual: A list: Low: look up, draft, remind; A yes: messages, records; People only: grades, discipline.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Sort jobs by the stakes. Looking things up, drafting a worksheet and your own reminders are low stakes. Messages to parents and changes to records need a named person’s yes. Some jobs stay with people: grades, discipline, decisions about a child.

scenes.visual: A list: The least data; Pupils’ details: only by rule; Prefer on the device; The law; children first.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Then data. Agents see the least data a job needs; pupils’ names, marks, health or family details only where a rule allows. Prefer tools that keep data on the device. Laws apply, such as Kenya’s and Egypt’s data protection laws, and children’s data needs the most care.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Cost is a fairness question too. A big cloud model uses about eighteen kilobytes a request, costs money and needs a signal. At twenty requests a day, that’s about eleven megabytes a month per teacher. A tiny model on the phone costs one download, then works offline.

scenes.visual: A list: No phone or data at home; Agent-only homework leaves pupils out; Always a paper way, at school.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Fairness also means pupils with no phone or data at home. Agent-only homework leaves them out. So anything an agent helps with must also be possible on paper, at school.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Quick check! A teacher wants an agent to write each pupil’s end-of-term report comment. Under a good policy, what happens?

scenes.visual: A list: The agent drafts; The teacher edits and signs; Names only by rule; The teacher is responsible.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: It may draft; the teacher reads, edits and signs each one. Names stay out of cloud tools unless a rule allows. And the teacher, not the agent, is responsible for every word.

scenes.visual: A list: Tell the named lead; Switch it off; Check the log; tell families; Fix, test, then switch on.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Plan for mistakes before they happen. Staff tell a named lead, who can switch the agent off. Check the log, and tell the families affected. Fix the cause, test again, then switch it back on.

scenes.visual: A list: Measure a request; Switch to 2G; Your data price; A month for all staff.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: App lab: what an agent costs
scenes.narration: In the app, measure a request on your phone, then switch to two G and compare the cloud. Set thirty requests a day and your data price, and work out a month for the whole staff.

scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Your turn. An agent sends a wrong message to parents. Who is responsible?

scenes.visual: Summary points: Six questions, answered; Least data, on the device; Count cost; keep a paper way.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.on_screen_text: Six questions, answered · Least data, on the device · Count cost; keep a paper way
scenes.narration: The school, through the person who approved it. Remember: a policy answers six questions. Keep data to the least, on the device where you can. Count the cost, and keep a paper way for every pupil.

scenes.visual: A list: Each group: one question; In their own words; Take it to the head teacher.
scenes.animation: Each item arrives as it is said.
scenes.narration: Try it in class tomorrow: let pupils help write the policy. Each group answers one of the six questions, in their own words. Then take their ideas, with your colleagues’, to your head teacher.

checkpoints.prompt: A teacher wants an agent to write each pupil’s end-of-term report comment. Under a good policy, what happens?

options.text: The agent writes and sends them
It may draft; the teacher reads, edits and signs each one

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — the agent can save time on a draft, but the teacher reads, edits and signs, and stays responsible.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — a report about a child is the teacher’s. The agent may draft; the teacher decides and signs.

checkpoints.prompt: An agent sends a wrong message to parents. Who is responsible?

options.text: The company that made the model
The school, through the person who approved it

checkpoints.feedback_correct: Correct — an agent can’t be responsible. The school is, through the named person who approved the message, and the log shows who.
checkpoints.feedback_wrong: Not quite — tools aren’t responsible, and the school chose to use it. The person who approved it answers for it.
